archetypes.name: Desperate Seller
tips: They need this done fast — a quick, certain closing timeline will move them more than squeezing the price.
Because they're anxious, staying calm and unhurried can quietly pull the number down.
Don't drag this out with lowball haggling — someone else's clean offer could win it out from under you.

archetypes.name: Proud Founder
archetypes.flavor: emotionally attached to the business and staff
tips: This is personal to them. Ask about the business's history before you talk numbers.
They care what happens to the people who work here. A credible plan for the staff buys room on price.
Aggressive undercutting will make them dig in. Patient, respectful framing works better than pressure.

archetypes.name: Relationship-Oriented Owner
tips: They value the relationship itself — reliability lands harder than an aggressive first offer.
Framing this as a long-term commitment, not a one-time transaction, is genuinely persuasive.
They remember if you've been transactional before. Consistency is real leverage.

archetypes.name: Corporate Divestment Committee
archetypes.flavor: an institutional seller, unmoved by personal appeals, focused on process and defensible valuation
tips: They don't respond to personal rapport — lead with clean numbers and a defensible valuation.
Process matters more than warmth. A clear, well-structured offer moves faster than a friendly one.
They will not move off their walk-away number for sentimental reasons.
